name: Digit Extraction
description: Use modulo 10 and division by 10 to peel digits from a number one by one.
commonMistakes: Forgetting that 0 has one digit
Dropping the last digit because the loop stops too early

name: Place Value Rebuild
description: Reconstruct a number from its digits by multiplying the current answer by 10 before adding the next digit.
commonMistakes: Appending digits in the wrong order
Forgetting to store the original value before mutating it

name: Numeric Palindrome
description: Compare a number with its reversed form to decide whether it reads the same both ways.
commonMistakes: Mutating the original number and then comparing against the changed value
Treating negative numbers as palindromes without a clear rule

name: Divisibility Check
description: Use modulo to decide whether one number divides another exactly.
commonMistakes: Checking the wrong modulo direction
Starting from 0 and triggering division by zero

name: Euclid GCD
description: Repeatedly replace (a, b) with (b, a % b) until the remainder becomes zero.
exampleJava: while (b != 0) { int r = a % b; a = b; b = r; }
commonMistakes: Not updating both variables in the right order
Stopping too early when the remainder is still non-zero

name: Factor Enumeration
description: Iterate through candidate divisors and collect the numbers that divide the target exactly.
commonMistakes: Missing the paired divisor n / d
Double-counting the square root when d * d == n

name: Primality Test
description: Reject non-primes by checking divisors only up to the square root of the number.
exampleJava: for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) if (n % d == 0) return false;
commonMistakes: Treating 1 as a prime number
Checking divisors all the way up to n instead of sqrt(n)

name: LCM from GCD
description: Use gcd(a, b) to compute lcm(a, b) efficiently with the identity a / gcd(a, b) * b.
commonMistakes: Multiplying before dividing and risking overflow unnecessarily
Using repeated addition instead of the gcd relation

name: Sieve Precomputation
description: Mark multiples of each prime candidate once so prime queries up to n become efficient.
exampleJava: for (int p = 2; p * p <= n; p++) if (isPrime[p]) for (int m = p * p; m <= n; m += p) isPrime[m] = false;
commonMistakes: Starting inner marking from 2 * p instead of p * p without understanding the cost
Forgetting to initialize 0 and 1 as non-prime

name: Modular Arithmetic
description: Keep intermediate values bounded by applying modulo after addition and multiplication where required.
commonMistakes: Applying modulo only at the very end after values have already grown too large
Forgetting to reduce the base before repeated multiplication

name: Fast Exponentiation
description: Use repeated squaring so exponentiation drops from linear time to logarithmic time.
exampleJava: while (exp > 0) { if ((exp & 1) == 1) ans = (ans * base) % mod; base = (base * base) % mod; exp >>= 1; }
commonMistakes: Multiplying the base exp times instead of halving the exponent
Forgetting to square the base when the exponent is reduced

name: Factorial Mod Precompute
description: Build factorial values incrementally while taking modulo at each step so future combinatorics queries can reuse them.
commonMistakes: Computing the full factorial before taking modulo
Starting the precompute loop from the wrong base case

name: Modular Inverse
description: Use Fermat-style exponentiation under a prime modulus to divide inside modular arithmetic safely.
commonMistakes: Using normal division instead of modular inverse
Forgetting that this shortcut assumes a prime modulus

name: nCr Mod Prime
description: Combine factorial precomputation and modular inverse so combinations can be computed efficiently under a prime modulus.
exampleJava: return fact[n] * invFact[r] % mod * invFact[n - r] % mod;
commonMistakes: Not handling r > n cleanly
Mixing integer division with modular arithmetic
